description:
Tune nextest worker concurrency from matched full-suite evidence so the opt-level-0 test profile uses this host efficiently without changing a test, assertion, or build profile.

## Background

The fixed runner currently uses nextest’s 24-worker host default. The opt-level-0 suite contains thousands of subprocess- and filesystem-heavy tests whose summed wall time does not establish CPU saturation, while setup scripts remain serialized. A bounded concurrency experiment can reduce the post-setup region without the rejected global optimization’s build regression, but excessive workers can increase contention, memory pressure, or flakiness and must not be accepted from one fast sample.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Compares the current 24-worker baseline with bounded 36-, 48-, and, only if useful and safe, 64-worker candidates on one already-built target under identical source, nextest 0.9.133, no-sccache, incremental-disabled, and setup-script conditions.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every measured run preserves the exact runnable and ignored identity sets with no missing or duplicate identities, all assertions pass, and setup time is reported separately from the post-setup test region.
- [hard] REQ-03: Accepts one fixed concurrency only after three consecutive full-suite samples each complete at or below 23,500 milliseconds, with no timeout, resource failure, order dependence, or selected-test duration regression above the committed 20-second final per-test bound.
- [hard] REQ-04: Records wall, aggregate test work, setup durations, peak memory or an equivalent host-pressure observation, and doctest control timing; rejects a faster candidate when memory pressure, flakiness, or doctest/suite-clock behavior makes it unsafe.
- [hard] REQ-05: If accepted, declares the chosen worker count once in the pinned nextest configuration and passes the profiler self-test, cargo-ci self-test, full suite, doctests, formatting, and configuration inspection; if rejected, records complete raw evidence and `no_change` without weakening any threshold.

## Notes

The experiment changes scheduling only. It must not add test groups that serialize or skip work, change retries/timeouts, alter the Rust build profile, or move setup or doctests outside the named suite clock.
title: Tune nextest worker concurrency
